page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES cryptography.

This instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage solutions for operating system and application data. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.c5.xlarge exhibits modest processing capabilities. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 25% performance tier. Memory performance is also constrained, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth registering at 20.58 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom 10% of tested configurations, and write bandwidth at 18.68 GB/sec.

Given its hardware profile, the instance is positioned as an entry-level compute-focused resource. It is suitable for lightweight compute tasks, basic web serving, or small-scale software compilation. However, intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, image processing, or text processing may encounter performance bottlenecks, as reflected in its lower-tier benchmark scores. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution for non-burstable tasks, though resource density remains low.
